title: Meta Q3 Earnings: Revenue Jumps 26% to $64.6 Billion as $9.9 Billion Legal Charge Cuts Profit
excerpt: Adjusted EPS of $7.40 beat the $6.52 estimate; reported EPS of $3.83 reflects the teen mental-health settlement charge, and AI capex pushed free cash flow negative.
body:
• Meta's third-quarter revenue rose 26% to $64.6 billion, beating the $63.4 billion consensus, as ad impressions grew 10% and average ad prices 14%.
  • Adjusted EPS of $7.40 topped the $6.52 estimate, but reported diluted EPS was $3.83 after a $9.89 billion charge for the multistate attorneys general settlement over teen mental health litigation.
  • Operating income fell 37% to $12.99 billion (it would have risen 11% without the charge), capex hit $34.91 billion in the quarter, and free cash flow was negative $2.12 billion.
  • Meta guided fourth-quarter revenue to $73–76 billion, raised full-year expenses to $175–179 billion, and proposed a new non-voting Class C share structure.

Meta Platforms delivered another quarter of rapid advertising growth on Wednesday, but the headline profit figures were dominated by a one-time legal charge of nearly $10 billion and an artificial intelligence spending bill that is now large enough to push quarterly free cash flow negative. The shares rose about 2% in after-hours trading.

Revenue for the quarter ended September 30 rose 26% year over year to $64.60 billion, ahead of the $63.41 billion consensus estimate, according to Zacks. Adjusted earnings per share were $7.40, comfortably above the $6.52 estimate. Reported diluted EPS, however, was $3.83, because third-quarter costs include a $9.89 billion charge tied to the agreement Meta announced in August with 52 state attorneys general to resolve litigation over teen mental health and social media, which provides for payments of up to roughly $18.59 billion. Excluding the charge, diluted EPS would have been $7.40 and operating income would have risen 11%.

The Cost of the AI Build-Out

Reported operating income fell 37% to $12.99 billion, a margin of 20% against 40% a year earlier, as total costs and expenses jumped 68% to $51.61 billion. Capital expenditure, including finance-lease payments, was $34.91 billion in the quarter alone, and free cash flow was negative $2.12 billion despite $32.79 billion of operating cash flow. Meta ended the quarter with $82.45 billion in cash and marketable securities and a headcount of 66,775, down 15% year over year. Net income was $9.86 billion, up sharply from a year-ago quarter that carried an unusually high tax charge.

Advertising Engine Still Running

The core business showed no sign of slowing. Family daily active people averaged 3.64 billion in September, up 3% year over year; ad impressions across the Family of Apps rose 10% and the average price per ad increased 14%. US and Canada advertising revenue grew 33%. Looking ahead, Meta guided fourth-quarter revenue to between $73 billion and $76 billion, kept full-year capital expenditure guidance at $135–145 billion, and raised its full-year expense outlook to $175–179 billion to reflect the legal settlement.

The board also approved a proposed non-voting Class C share structure, with a conditional one-for-one distribution of Class C shares to existing Class A and Class B holders that would leave current shareholders' voting power unchanged. For the company's large Indian user base — India is Meta's biggest market by users across Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp — the results underline how much of the group's growth, and its regulatory exposure, now sits outside the United States even as the spending is concentrated in American AI data centres.
